newsitem.title: FINLAND: Boliden aims to expand zinc, copper operations.
newsitem.headline: Boliden aims to expand zinc, copper operations.

text.p: Boliden Ltd is aiming to expand its zinc and copper operations while boosting exploration and acquisitions, president and CEO Anders Bulow said on Wednesday.
"International growth is at the top of our agenda," he told delegates at the Metal Bulletin base metal concentrates conference.
Among projects in the works, Boliden was currently drilling on its Renstrom zinc mine in northern Sweden, the company's richest base metal find with a resource of two million tonnes, he said.
The find contained an estimated average grade of 13 percent zinc, 4.5 grams per tonne of gold and 270 grams of silver, and also included some copper and lead.
Over the next nine to 12 months Boliden would spend $2.5 million to delineate the ore body, he added.
Boliden's Los Frailes zinc mine in Spain was due to come on stream in the fourth quarter of 1997 with an expected 125,000-tonne annual output, he said.
"We anticipate rapid expansion thereafter," he added.
On the smelting side, the company's Ronnskar copper smelter in Sweden was in the process of a final feasibility study to expand capacity by 100,000 tonnes from a current 130,000 tonnes.
The anticipated investment would be $200 million, and the cash/cost on incremental tonnages seven cents per pound of copper, Bulow said.
"We hope to have the final feasibility in very early 1998 and start expansion in 1998 and it would be onstream by 2001," he said.

Boliden's jointly-owned Norzink smelter was also pegged for expansion following a board decision last week to do a pre-feasibility study into a 100,000-tonne expansion of zinc smelting capacity, Bulow said.

"Our long-term ambition for our key commodities is to strike a balance between our mining and smelting capacities. Short-term we have excess mining capacity on zinc and excess smelting on copper," Bulow said on the sidelines of the conference.
"Neither of those is a problem, but its part of a rationale for expanding the Norzink operation and it produces more of a incentive to get involved in copper mining projects."

The company was also investing more money into exploration -- pegged at $25 million this year, compared to an exploration budget of $10 million in 1994 -- and was looking into acquisitions with a focus on copper and zinc.
Bulow gave no details of potential corporate deals, but added: "We have a lot of financial muscle to play with but we don't want to go overboard."
Boliden was listed on the Toronto and Montreal stock exchanges this month, which Bulow said would help the company grow at a much faster rate than otherwise.
